ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, CD is the median of the base of the isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$, BE bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects CD at point E. Given that AC = 8 and DE = 2, what is the area of $\triangle BCE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct EF $\perp$ BC at F, \\
since AC = BC = 8, and CD is the median of the isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$ on the base, \\
therefore CD $\perp$ AB, \\
since BE bisects $\angle ABC$, ED $\perp$ AB, and EF $\perp$ BC, \\
therefore EF = DE = 2, \\
thus, the area of $\triangle BCE$ = $\frac{1}{2} \times BC \times EF = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 2 = \boxed{8}$.
